nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates a small set of runways to inbound aircraft. Each aircraft that wants to land first reads the current version stamp of a chosen runway and remembers it, without yet committing. It then attempts to claim that runway optimistically: the claim succeeds only if the runway is still free and its version stamp has not changed since the read, at which point the runway's occupant is set to that aircraft and its version stamp is bumped. If the runway was taken or its stamp moved, the aircraft abandons the attempt and retries from scratch later. An aircraft that has claimed a runway lands and eventually releases it, freeing the runway and bumping the stamp again. Aircraft may be arbitrarily slow between reading and claiming, but never fail outright, so a stale read simply forces a retry rather than a deadlock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct aircraft ever simultaneously occupy the same runway.

  Cap = 3
INIT Init

INVARIANT WithinCapacity
CONSTRAINT TermBound
nl:
A distributed library reservation service runs on several server nodes, one of which acts as the elected leader for a popular book that has a fixed number of lendable copies. Only the current leader may issue reservation grants, and it stamps each grant with its election term. When the leader fails, a surviving node elects itself leader by advancing to a strictly higher term. The leader issues a reservation grant only when the number of already-confirmed reservations plus the number of grants still in flight is below the copy limit. Grant messages travel over an asynchronous network and may be delivered in any order, not necessarily the order sent; delivering a grant confirms one reservation. A patron may later cancel, freeing one confirmed reservation. Stale grants from an old term are ignored on delivery.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of confirmed reservations plus grants still in flight never exceeds the fixed number of copies.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Banks = {a, b, c}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
An interbank settlement service maintains one shared settlement record whose numeric value is updated concurrently by several member banks during a batch. Each bank first reads a snapshot of the record's current value together with its epoch number. To commit its contribution, the bank re-checks that the epoch has not advanced since its snapshot; only then does it write the incremented value and advance the epoch by one. If the epoch moved, the bank's snapshot is stale and it abandons the write and rereads, so no earlier update is silently overwritten. A settlement operator may reconfigure the batch by advancing the epoch without changing the value, which forces in-progress banks to reread. A privileged administrator may additionally force a direct adjustment to the record, advancing the epoch, bypassing the snapshot check.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the record's value always equals the number of banks whose contributions have committed plus the number of administrator adjustments, so no committed update is ever lost.

A print shop runs a job spooler as a small cluster of coordinator nodes, exactly one of which is the elected leader at any time, identified by an ever-increasing election term. Print jobs begin pending. Only the leader may dispatch a pending job onto a free physical press, which records that the press now holds that job. A press then physically prints the job it holds, an irreversible act that consumes paper and toner; printing marks the job printed and frees the press. A dispatched job cannot be dispatched again because its stage is no longer pending, and a printed job is never sitting on any press, so it can never be printed a second time even if the leader fails and a new leader with a higher term takes over mid-batch. Coordinator nodes may be arbitrarily slow but do not corrupt state; the current leader may also step down, after which a survivor is elected.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every print job is physically printed at most once, because a printed job is never held by any press.

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyHolderCharges
CONSTRAINT GrantBound
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots shares a single charging bay that only one robot may physically occupy at a time. Coordination uses a rotating token that circulates around the robots arranged in a fixed logical ring. A robot that needs to charge first raises a request. It may begin charging only while it currently holds the token, moving into the charging state. When done, it stops charging and becomes idle again. The token advances to the next robot in the ring only when its current holder is idle, never while that holder is charging. A privileged warehouse administrator may override the rotation and hand the token directly to any chosen robot, but only when no robot is currently charging, so the override never interrupts an in-progress charge.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at any moment at most one robot is charging, because only the robot currently holding the token may be in the charging state.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  N = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OneConfigurer
CONSTRAINT OverrideBound
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network has several lock controllers that share one configuration hub. Only one controller may reconfigure the hub at a time. The right to reconfigure circulates as a numeric token position that names one controller's ring index. A controller that needs to push new settings first flags its intent. It may begin reconfiguring only while the token position equals its own index, entering an active configuring state; when finished it returns to standby. The token position advances by one around the ring, modulo the number of controllers, only while the controller it currently points at is in standby, never while that controller is configuring. A privileged administrator holding the master key may jump the token position directly to any controller's index, but only while no controller is actively configuring, so no configuration in progress is ever disturbed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one controller is in the active configuring state at any time, since a controller configures only when the token position points at its own index.

An elevator bank in a skyscraper handles hall calls placed at floors. A dispatcher role runs on several controller nodes, exactly one of which is the elected leader, marked by an increasing term. Each hall call starts pending. Only the leader may assign a pending call to one specific elevator car, recording that car as the call's sole owner and marking the call assigned. The assigned car then starts serving the call, and later finishes it, marking the call served. A call that is already assigned cannot be assigned again because it is no longer pending, so it can never be handed to a second car, even when the leader fails and a new leader with a higher term resumes dispatching. Controller nodes may be arbitrarily slow yet never corrupt state, and the leader may step down, after which a survivor is elected.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no hall call is ever served by two different elevator cars, because a car serves a call only if it is that call's recorded owner.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cars = {a, b, c}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OneInShaft
CONSTRAINT EpochBound
nl:
An elevator bank contains one express shaft that only a single car may occupy at a time. A controller grants access using epoch numbers. A car that wants the express shaft raises a request. The controller issues a grant stamped with the current epoch, sent over an asynchronous network where grants may arrive in any order. A car enters the express shaft upon receiving a grant whose epoch matches the current epoch and only while the shaft is unoccupied; entering marks the car as inside. The car later exits, freeing the shaft. The controller may reconfigure the system by advancing the epoch, after which any still-undelivered grant from an older epoch is stale and is discarded on arrival rather than admitting a car.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one car occupies the express shaft at any moment.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  NumCranes = 3
  Cap = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
CONSTRAINT OverrideBound
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has several cranes that feed one shared staging buffer with a fixed maximum number of container slots. Only the crane currently holding a circulating token may add a container. A crane that has a container ready flags its intent. While it holds the token and the buffer is below its capacity, it deposits one container, raising the buffer occupancy. Separately, ground trucks continually haul containers away, lowering the buffer occupancy whenever it is above zero. The token advances by one around the ring of cranes, letting the next crane take a turn. A privileged yard administrator may override the rotation and hand the token to any chosen crane. Deposits are refused whenever the buffer is already full.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of containers in the staging buffer never exceeds its fixed capacity.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  TotalSlots = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
CONSTRAINT TermBound
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed pool of identical landing slots. A dispatcher role runs on several controllers, exactly one of which is the elected leader, marked by an increasing term. Every slot is in exactly one of three places: available in the pool, in flight as an unacknowledged grant, or occupied by a landed aircraft. Only the leader may grant a slot, which moves one unit from the available pool into an in-flight grant message. Grant messages travel asynchronously and may be delivered in any order; delivering a grant moves that unit from in-flight into occupied. When an aircraft departs, its unit moves from occupied back into the available pool. The leader may step down and a survivor is elected with a higher term, but leadership changes neither create nor destroy slots.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of slots, counting available plus in-flight grants plus occupied, always equals the fixed pool size.

A hospital operating-room scheduler lets surgeons book fixed operating-room time slots. Each slot carries a version stamp and an owner, initially unowned. A surgeon who wants a slot first reads that slot, recording it as the target and remembering its version stamp, without committing. To confirm, the surgeon re-checks that the slot is still unowned and that its version stamp has not changed since the read; only then does the surgeon become the recorded owner and the slot's version stamp is bumped. If the slot was taken or its stamp moved, the surgeon abandons and rereads. A surgeon holding a slot may cancel, freeing it and bumping the stamp. A privileged administrator may directly assign an unowned slot to any surgeon, bypassing the version check, and only ever assigns a slot that is currently unowned.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every surgeon shown as having booked a slot is in fact that slot's recorded owner, so no slot is ever double-booked.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
  Chutes = {c1, c2}
  Cap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
An airport baggage router directs bags into a set of chutes, each with a fixed capacity. Routing decisions are made by a cluster of controller nodes that vote. To admit a bag into a chute, one node opens a proposal naming the target chute, but only while that chute is below capacity. Other nodes then cast votes for the open proposal. Once the proposal has collected votes from a strict majority quorum of the nodes and the chute is still below capacity, the admission commits, increasing that chute's load by one and closing the proposal. A proposal may instead be aborted, closing it without admitting anything. Independently, downstream handling removes a bag from any non-empty chute. Nodes may be arbitrarily slow to vote but do not fail, so a proposal simply waits until enough votes arrive.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no chute ever holds more bags than its fixed capacity.

A subway signalling system divides the track into fixed blocks, each of which may hold at most one train at a time. Signal authority runs on several interlocking controllers, exactly one of which is the elected leader marked by an increasing term. A train not currently on any block may enter an empty block only with the leader's authority, which records that train as the block's owner and places the train on it. A train on a block may leave, clearing its owner and removing itself from the block. A train that is already on a block cannot enter another until it leaves. When the leader fails, a survivor is elected with a higher term and resumes granting. A privileged dispatcher may override the signalling and place a train onto an empty block directly, but only onto a block that has no owner.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a train is physically on a block, it is that block's recorded owner, so no block ever holds two different trains.

A container-ship crane yard seals containers, an irreversible act. Sealing a container in a given slot requires two nested locks acquired in order: first a coarse lock on the whole bay, then a fine lock on the specific slot. A crane begins idle. It first takes the coarse bay lock, which only one crane may hold. While holding the coarse lock it takes the fine lock on an unsealed target slot. Only then, still holding both locks, may it seal that slot, which permanently marks the slot sealed. Afterwards the crane releases both locks and returns to idle, freeing the bay for another crane. Cranes may be arbitrarily slow between steps but never fail, so a partially locked crane simply holds its locks until it proceeds. A slot that is already sealed cannot be fine-locked for sealing again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: a slot is sealed at most once, because the fine lock needed to seal it is only ever held by the single crane that also holds the coarse bay lock.

Two independent controller instances, a phone app and a wall hub, share one common pool of smart door locks and may each flash new firmware to a lock, an irreversible act. Flashing is guarded by a two-level nested lock over the shared pool. At any moment at most one instance holds the pool: an instance with pending work first takes the coarse pool lock, raising the lock level to one. Holding the coarse lock, it then fine-locks one target door from the shared pool that has not yet been flashed, raising the level to two. Only at level two may it flash the target door, permanently recording that door as flashed. It then unlocks everything, dropping the level to zero and releasing the pool for the other instance. Because the two instances contend for the same single coarse pool lock, they can never both be mid-flash at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: a door is flashed at most once, since flashing requires level two, which in turn requires sole ownership of the shared coarse pool lock.

Two independent spooler instances, a desktop client and a server daemon, share one common pool of printers, and only the currently elected leader may drive the pool. Leadership is tracked by an ever-increasing global election term; when a new leader is elected, the term advances and the new leader's local term is set to match it. Only an instance that is the current leader and whose local term equals the global term may claim control of the shared printer pool, recording itself as the pool's controller. While it controls the pool, that same instance may dispatch print work. It later releases the pool. Because a superseded instance no longer has a local term equal to the global term, it can neither claim nor drive the pool, so a stale instance can never act on the shared pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the shared printer pool has a controller, that controller is the current leader, so no stale or unauthorized instance ever drives the pool.

CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
Two independent spooler instances, a desktop client and a server daemon, share one common pool of printers, and only the currently elected leader may drive the pool. Leadership is tracked by an ever-increasing global election term; when a new leader is elected, the term advances and the new leader's local term is set to match it. Only an instance that is the current leader and whose local term equals the global term may claim control of the shared printer pool, recording itself as the pool's controller; electing a new leader immediately voids any previous instance's control of the pool. While it controls the pool, that same instance may dispatch print work. It later releases the pool. Because a superseded instance no longer has a local term equal to the global term, it can neither claim nor drive the pool, so a stale instance can never act on the shared pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the shared printer pool has a controller, that controller is the current leader, so no stale or unauthorized instance ever drives the pool.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Total = 3
  MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FleetConserved
CONSTRAINT EpochBound
nl:
An elevator bank owns a fixed fleet of elevator cars. At any time each car is in exactly one of three states: parked in the lobby, moving in service, or out in maintenance. A parked car may depart into service, but only while the number of moving cars is below the current service capacity. A moving car may arrive, returning to parked. A parked car may be pulled out for maintenance, and a car in maintenance may be returned to parked. A building operator may reconfigure the bank by advancing an epoch counter and setting a new service capacity within allowed bounds; this capacity limit can rise or fall at runtime and only constrains future departures. Reconfiguration never adds or removes cars from the fleet. The three state counts therefore always sum to the fixed fleet size.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of parked, moving, and maintenance cars always sums to the fixed total fleet size, so no car is ever created or destroyed.

A library reservation service guards one shared holds-record with a lease. At most one node may hold the lease at a time, and each grant stamps the lease with a fresh, increasing epoch that is also recorded as that node's held epoch. Only the node currently holding the lease, and whose held epoch still matches the live lease epoch, may write the holds-record, recording itself as the record's current writer. A held lease may lapse: expiry advances the lease epoch, clears the holder, and clears the record's writer, so any node whose held epoch is now behind is fenced out and can no longer write. A node may also voluntarily release its lease, which likewise advances the epoch and clears the writer. One node may crash silently at any time, after which it takes no further actions; its lease, if any, simply lingers until it expires.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the holds-record has a current writer, that writer is the live lease holder whose held epoch matches the current lease epoch, so no stale or unauthorized node ever writes.

CONSTRAINT EpochBound

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Instances = {engineA, engineB}
  Cap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
CONSTRAINT TermBound
nl:
Two independent settlement engine instances share a single pool of settlement slots with a fixed capacity. Only the currently elected leader may post settlements into the shared pool. Leadership is tracked by an increasing global term; electing a leader advances the term and sets the new leader's local term to match. An instance may post a settlement only when it is the leader, its local term equals the global term, and the pool still has free capacity; posting raises the pool occupancy by one. A clearing bank independently drains one settled slot whenever the pool is non-empty, lowering occupancy. The leader may step down, after which a survivor is elected with a higher term. Because posting is gated on free capacity, the pool never overflows regardless of which instance leads or how leadership changes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of occupied settlement slots never exceeds the pool's fixed capacity.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Stations = {t1, t2}
  Total = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SlotsConserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator holds a fixed pool of identical landing slots and grants them one at a time through a two-phase commit run by a coordinator across all participating tower stations. Every slot is in exactly one of three places: available in the pool, in transit as part of an active transaction, or allocated to a flight. To begin, the coordinator prepares a transaction, moving one slot from available into in-transit and opening a vote round. Each tower station casts its vote independently, and votes may arrive in any order. Once every station has voted yes, the coordinator commits, moving the in-transit slot into allocated. If the coordinator instead aborts, the in-transit slot returns to available. An allocated slot is later freed back into the pool when its flight departs. No phase ever creates or destroys a slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of available plus in-transit plus allocated slots always equals the fixed pool size.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  Cap = 2
  Tokens = {k1, k2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
CONSTRAINT VerBound
nl:
A print shop spooler lets several worker threads enqueue jobs into one shared bounded print queue using optimistic concurrency. The queue tracks a length and a version stamp. A worker first reads a snapshot of the current version stamp. To enqueue, it re-checks that the version stamp has not moved since its read and that the queue is below its fixed capacity; only then does it append a job, raising the length and bumping the version. If the version moved, its snapshot is stale and it rereads. The press prints one queued job whenever the queue is non-empty, lowering the length, bumping the version, and emitting a completion token. Completion tokens are acknowledged by the front desk in any order, not necessarily the order printed. Enqueue is refused whenever the queue is already full.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the print queue length never exceeds its fixed capacity.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  NumEngines = 2
  Slots = {sa, sb}
  Orders = {o1, o2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PairingConsistent
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction is cleared by two matching-engine instances that share one common pool of fill slots. The right to allocate circulates as a token around the two engines. An order first submits, marking itself as pending. The engine currently holding the token may allocate one free fill slot from the shared pool to one pending order, recording the slot's owner as that order and recording the order's assigned slot; this pairs the slot and the order one to one. A filled order may later be released, freeing its slot back into the pool and clearing the pairing. The token advances around the ring so the other engine gets a turn. Because a slot is allocated only while free and an order is allocated only while pending and unpaired, the slot-to-order pairing stays a consistent one-to-one matching.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no fill slot is ever allocated to two different orders, since each owned slot and its order point at each other exactly.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2}
  Seats = {sa, sb}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatConsistent
CONSTRAINT GenBound
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker assigns players to seats using optimistic concurrency over the whole lobby. The lobby carries a single generation counter that advances on every successful change. A player begins idle. It picks a target seat and records a snapshot of the lobby generation, entering a picking state. To claim, it re-checks that the generation has not advanced since its snapshot and that the target seat is still empty; only then does it take the seat, become seated, and advance the generation. If the generation moved or the seat was taken, its snapshot is stale and it returns to idle to try again. A seated player may leave, freeing its seat and advancing the generation. Players may be arbitrarily slow between picking and claiming but never fail, so a stale snapshot merely forces another attempt.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every seated player genuinely owns the seat it picked, so no seat is ever assigned to two different players.

A network of vending controllers guards each dispense, an irreversible act, behind a quorum vote. Each product selection is paid for at most once. To dispense a paid, not-yet-dispensed selection, one controller opens a vote proposal naming that selection; only one proposal is open at a time. Other controllers cast votes for the open proposal, and they may be arbitrarily slow but never fail, so the proposal simply waits for votes. Once a strict majority quorum of controllers has voted, the selection is dispensed, permanently marking it dispensed and closing the proposal. A proposal may instead be cancelled, closing it with nothing dispensed. Because a proposal can only open on a paid selection that has not been dispensed, and dispensing marks it, no selection is ever dispensed twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every dispensed selection was paid for, and no open proposal ever targets an already-dispensed selection, so no product is dispensed more than once.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {s1, s2, s3}
  MaxSeats = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatAllocation
nl:
A university course-registration system seats students into one course backed by a compare-and-swap register that holds the index of the next free seat. Seat indices are handed out in increasing order. A student begins idle. It reads a snapshot of the next-seat register, entering a reading state. To enroll, it performs a compare-and-swap: it commits only if the register still equals its snapshot and the next-seat index is below the current capacity. On success it takes exactly that seat index as its own, the register advances by one, and the student becomes enrolled. If the register moved since the snapshot, the compare-and-swap fails and the student rereads. A registrar may raise or lower the course capacity at runtime; lowering capacity never revokes seats already taken, it only stops further enrollment.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every enrolled student owns a distinct seat below the next-seat index, so no seat index is ever assigned to two students.
